subject.title: PR5/5 durable core: internal session delivery handoff

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this opt-in durable-runtime, shared-state, Gateway API, CLI, and plugin-SDK surface as a supported core product boundary?
rationale: The patch introduces permanent storage, environment, protocol, SDK, runtime-worker, and operational semantics that cannot be accepted solely from implementation correctness or contributor proof.

options.title: Sponsor the durable stack
options.body: Approve the core product direction, require exact-head reset and upgrade proof, then review and land the ordered predecessor stack before this final handoff.

options.title: Pause pending sponsorship
options.body: Keep the PR unmerged until a maintainer explicitly owns the durable-runtime scope, supported lifecycle, compatibility contract, and release plan.

options.title: Decline the core surface
options.body: Close the stack and revisit only a narrower capability after a maintainer-approved architecture identifies the minimum missing core seam.

recommendation.title: Pause pending sponsorship
recommendation.body: Keep the PR unmerged until a maintainer explicitly owns the durable-runtime scope, supported lifecycle, compatibility contract, and release plan.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work introduced the session-delivery queue reused by this design, making them the strongest available history-based owner for routing the session-generation and queue contract decision.
